other_side: NLW's lead is that the revolt has little to do with AI: it is about agency, NDAs and broken promises, and it can be answered by builders engaging communities openly and paying generously for local buy-in. Zitron's argument cuts underneath that. He reads the same build-out as a debt-funded asset bubble, financed through special purpose vehicles and variable interest entities that keep hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of obligations off hyperscaler balance sheets, against Bloomberg's estimate of over five hundred billion dollars in outstanding AI data centre debt. On his numbers the capacity being planned needs roughly $435bn a year in compute revenue to make sense, while actual spend is nearer $100bn and comes overwhelmingly from OpenAI, Anthropic and the hyperscalers funding them. His conclusion is that data centre construction is "a debt-funded asset bubble with ruinous consequences" — which would make local distrust not a communications failure but a correct reading of the deal.
truth_beneath: Both men orbit one variable: how much of the announced build-out will ever be built and paid for. They agree on more than the tone suggests — that ERCOT's 474-gigawatt queue is padded with speculative and duplicate filings, and that communities have sound historical reason to disbelieve job promises. The empirical question is attrition, and the observable that settles it is the conversion rate from interconnection request to energised, revenue-generating capacity, alongside the first restructuring or impairment of a data centre special purpose vehicle. The residue is pure worldview: whether local distrust is a communications failure that better engagement can repair, or an accurate reading of an unsound financial scheme. Whittemore is vindicated if projects that negotiate openly and pay generously get built and the promised benefits arrive; Zitron if a large share stalls and the debt is impaired. Both are polemicists with incentives — Whittemore bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — and the signal is that both call the queue substantially fictional. Watch what Abbott's ERCOT audit publishes about withdrawals.
